assets.name: Secure Bootloader
assets.description: Primary bootloader responsible for verifying the authenticity and integrity of firmware images before execution on any compute tier (HPC, Gateway, Zonal Controller, or Classic ECU).

safety.rationale: Bootloader compromise creates fleet-wide financial/operational exposure (recall, rootkit remediation) rather than a direct physical safety effect on the OEM itself.

financial.rationale: Compromise allows fleet-wide persistent rootkits, requiring massive physical recall and component replacement.

operational.rationale: Loss of a trusted boot chain undermines the OEM’s ability to guarantee authentic firmware fleet-wide, halting safe OTA operations until remediated.

privacy.rationale: Bootloader compromise does not itself expose personal data.

safety.rationale: Verifies firmware authenticity at boot; a compromise enables execution of unauthorized firmware but does not itself actuate any vehicle function - the safety effect depends entirely on what a subsequently loaded payload does.

financial.rationale: No direct financial exposure to the individual road user from a boot-chain compromise.

operational.rationale: A corrupted boot chain can leave any ECU it protects unbootable, disabling vehicle functions until serviced.

privacy.rationale: Bootloader compromise does not itself expose personal data.

assets.name: Device Private Key / Root of Trust
assets.description: Cryptographic private key securely fused in physical hardware (HSM, TPM, or TEE) used for component identity, secure boot, and cryptographic handshakes.

safety.rationale: Key compromise drives OEM financial/operational exposure (forged firmware, cloned modules) rather than a direct physical safety effect on the OEM.

financial.rationale: Key compromise breaks the trust anchor, allowing attackers to forge legitimate signed firmware updates or clone physical modules.

operational.rationale: Loss of the root-of-trust key forces fleet-wide re-provisioning or hardware replacement to restore a trustworthy identity chain.

privacy.rationale: Key material can be linked to a specific module/vehicle identity, so its disclosure has a privacy dimension for the OEM’s device-identity database.

safety.rationale: Enables forging of signed firmware or cloning of module identity, which could subsequently be used to target safety-critical ECUs; the key itself does not actuate any function - a further malicious firmware delivery and execution step is required.

financial.rationale: No direct financial exposure to the individual road user.

operational.rationale: Cloned or forged module identities can disrupt the affected vehicle’s ability to complete authenticated operations (e.g., updates, secure sessions).

privacy.rationale: Device identity keys are not directly linked to personal data of the vehicle occupant.

assets.name: Operating System Kernel
assets.description: The base runtime operating system layer (RTOS or Rich OS) managing hardware resources, execution tasks, and process isolation boundaries.

safety.rationale: Kernel compromise is reflected in OEM financial/operational impact (remediation, liability) rather than a direct physical safety effect on the OEM.

financial.rationale: Kernel-level compromise on any node typically necessitates a full re-flash/re-certification of the affected platform across the fleet.

operational.rationale: Kernel compromise causes complete loss of control over the node's behavior.

privacy.rationale: A compromised kernel can be leveraged to access any process’s data on that node, including cached user data.

safety.rationale: The kernel is a generic runtime layer used across both safety-critical and non-safety-critical compute nodes; its compromise can disrupt or halt tasks on that node, but the resulting safety effect depends entirely on which application (if any safety-critical one) is hosted on the affected node.

financial.rationale: No direct financial exposure to the individual road user.

operational.rationale: A crashed or hijacked kernel halts all tasks on that compute node, disabling whatever function it hosts until reset or repair.

privacy.rationale: No direct exposure of personal data from a kernel-level fault alone.

assets.name: Vehicle Access Authorization Token
assets.description: Ephemeral cryptographic security keys or tokens authorizing vehicle unlocking, physical entry, and immobilization override (covers PEPS, PaaK, and smart fobs).

safety.rationale: Token compromise drives OEM financial/reputational exposure (theft liability) rather than a direct physical safety effect on the OEM.

financial.rationale: Results in reputational damage and potential liability for easily stolen vehicles.

operational.rationale: Drives a rise in warranty/dealer service requests and potential recall campaign for the affected component.

privacy.rationale: Access tokens do not themselves carry personal data beyond device pairing identifiers.

safety.rationale: Unauthorized entry/immobilization override enables vehicle theft but does not itself actuate any function that could injure the occupant or other road users while driving.

financial.rationale: Token sniffing or replay attacks bypass physical barriers, enabling complete vehicle theft.

operational.rationale: Loss of primary transportation.

privacy.rationale: The token itself does not carry personal profile data.

assets.name: In-Vehicle User Profile and PII Data
assets.description: User-specific personal data stored locally within the vehicle compute environment, including navigation history, sync maps, contact directories, and cloud application credentials.

safety.rationale: PII exposure carries OEM regulatory/financial exposure, not a direct physical safety effect.

financial.rationale: Data breach notification, regulatory fines, and customer-trust remediation costs following a PII exposure.

operational.rationale: Requires incident response, credential rotation for affected users, and potential feature suspension.

privacy.rationale: Large-scale data breaches compromise regulatory compliance frameworks (GDPR/CCPA), leading to severe fines.

safety.rationale: Exposure of personal data does not itself create a physical safety hazard for the vehicle occupant.

financial.rationale: No direct financial loss from the data exposure itself, though it may enable downstream identity-theft attempts.

operational.rationale: No direct effect on the vehicle’s operation.

privacy.rationale: Exposure of home addresses, travel patterns, and personal contact graphs.

assets.name: Machine Learning Perception Weights & Models
assets.description: Deep learning network configuration layers, object detection models, and neural network weights used to classify environmental features (lanes, signs, targets). Shared by specialized edge sensors or central ADAS accelerators.

safety.rationale: Model exfiltration/tampering exposes the OEM to IP loss and liability, not a direct physical safety effect on the OEM itself.

financial.rationale: Exfiltration of proprietary neural network weights represents massive intellectual property loss for the OEM.

operational.rationale: A poisoned or reverted model requires fleet-wide OTA redistribution and re-validation before ADAS features can be safely re-enabled.

privacy.rationale: Model weights do not themselves contain personal data.

safety.rationale: Poisoned or corrupted weights degrade perception accuracy, which can contribute to a missed-detection event; the model itself does not actuate any function - the effect passes through the separate planning and control logic before reaching a physical outcome.

financial.rationale: No direct financial exposure to the individual road user.

operational.rationale: Degraded perception accuracy can disable or restrict ADAS features until the model is restored.

privacy.rationale: Model weights do not themselves contain personal data.

assets.name: Automated Driving Trajectory Planning Algorithm
assets.description: Decision-making application binaries that ingest sensor fusion telemetry and output the lateral and longitudinal control setpoints sent to actuation.

safety.rationale: Trajectory-logic compromise is reflected in OEM financial/operational liability exposure rather than a direct physical safety effect on the OEM.

financial.rationale: A defect or compromise in trajectory planning logic exposes the OEM to product-liability claims and a potential safety recall of the automated-driving feature.

operational.rationale: Requires immediate feature suspension and validated patch rollout across the fleet.

privacy.rationale: Trajectory planning logic does not process personal data.

safety.rationale: The algorithm directly computes the lateral/longitudinal control setpoints sent to actuation; corrupting its logic directly commands the vehicle into an unsafe physical path with no further exploitation of another asset required.

financial.rationale: No direct financial exposure to the individual road user.

operational.rationale: A faulted planning algorithm disables the automated-driving feature until restored.

privacy.rationale: Trajectory planning logic does not process personal data.

assets.name: OTA Update Orchestration Middleware
assets.description: Software lifecycle middleware coordinating package download, integrity and signature verification, and flashing choreography across target ECUs and sub-buses.

safety.rationale: OTA compromise translates into OEM financial/operational exposure (mass recall, remediation), not a direct physical safety effect on the OEM.

financial.rationale: Failure of OTA mechanisms prevents the OEM from patching security flaws or deploying feature updates, leading to mass physical recalls.

operational.rationale: Loss of the OTA channel removes the OEM’s primary remote remediation path for security and safety patches fleet-wide.

privacy.rationale: The orchestration middleware itself does not process personal data.

safety.rationale: A compromised orchestrator can push unauthorized code to any ECU it targets, but a further step - crafting and successfully flashing a malicious payload to a specific safety-critical ECU - is required before any physical effect occurs.

financial.rationale: No direct financial exposure to the individual road user.

operational.rationale: A compromised or disabled OTA channel can leave the vehicle unable to receive functional or security updates.

privacy.rationale: The orchestration middleware itself does not process personal data.

assets.name: Wireless Wide-Area Network (WWAN) Communication Channel
assets.description: The cellular radio frequency connection (4G/5G/6G) link establishing data transport pipelines between the vehicle's network coordinator and external telematics base stations.

safety.rationale: Loss of cellular connectivity affects OEM operational/financial telemetry visibility, not a direct physical safety effect on the OEM.

financial.rationale: Represents ongoing carrier/service costs and lost telemetry-driven revenue opportunities.

operational.rationale: Loss of telemetry data from the fleet.

privacy.rationale: The channel carries user and vehicle telemetry that could be intercepted if confidentiality is broken.

safety.rationale: Loss of cellular infrastructure breaks automated emergency tracking and safety eCall applications.

financial.rationale: No direct financial exposure to the individual road user.

operational.rationale: Loss of the cellular channel disables remote services (remote start/climate, cloud navigation, fleet telemetry) for the affected vehicle.

privacy.rationale: The channel carries location and usage telemetry that could be exposed if confidentiality is broken.

assets.name: Central Network Routing & Firewall Rules
assets.description: Configuration matrices, access control lists (ACLs), and frame forwarding rules separating security domains over CAN matrices or Ethernet VLANs.

safety.rationale: Routing/firewall compromise is reflected in OEM financial/operational exposure, not a direct physical safety effect on the OEM.

financial.rationale: Loss of network segmentation integrity requires a fleet-wide security posture review and remediation, with associated liability exposure.

operational.rationale: Corrupted routing rules can misdirect or block critical inter-domain traffic fleet-wide.

privacy.rationale: Routing configuration data does not itself carry personal data.

safety.rationale: Corrupting these rules permits unauthorized lateral movement from low-trust to safety-critical domains, but a further step - actually crafting and injecting malicious messages once that access is gained - is required before any physical effect occurs.

financial.rationale: No direct financial exposure to the individual road user.

operational.rationale: Corrupted routing rules can silently drop or misroute traffic needed for normal vehicle functions.

privacy.rationale: Routing configuration data does not itself carry personal data.

assets.name: Type-1 Hypervisor Platform
assets.description: Hardware-level hypervisor partitioning execution environments into safe, highly isolated virtual machines on high-performance compute nodes.

safety.rationale: Hypervisor compromise is reflected in OEM financial/operational exposure, not a direct physical safety effect on the OEM.

financial.rationale: A hypervisor-level compromise undermines the isolation guarantees the OEM’s entire consolidated-compute architecture depends on, requiring platform-wide remediation.

operational.rationale: Loss of hypervisor integrity can take down every guest partition it hosts on that compute node.

privacy.rationale: A hypervisor breakout can expose data from any co-hosted guest partition, including infotainment user data.

safety.rationale: A hypervisor jailbreak can starve or crash adjacent guest partitions, but the resulting safety effect depends on whether a safety-critical task happens to be co-hosted on the same physical node - this is a resource-isolation failure, not itself an actuation of any vehicle function.

financial.rationale: No direct financial exposure to the individual road user.

operational.rationale: A hypervisor fault can crash every guest OS partition running on the affected compute node.

privacy.rationale: Hypervisor-level compromise alone does not directly expose road-user personal data (that risk sits with the guest OS/app it hosts).

assets.name: OEM & Fleet Operations Back-End API Interface
assets.description: Web service gateway (REST/gRPC API) through which the vehicle platform exchanges operational metrics, state configuration, and remote orchestration commands with OEM backend infrastructure.

safety.rationale: API compromise is reflected in OEM financial/operational exposure, not a direct physical safety effect on the OEM.

financial.rationale: No Fleet-Wide-scale threat in the catalog compromises this interface directly (BOLA-class threats abuse an already-valid session's authorization, they don't breach the gateway itself); realistic exposure is bounded to the API tenant/campaign affected, driving SLA penalties and remediation cost rather than fleet-wide revenue disruption.

operational.rationale: Degrades operational visibility for the affected API tenant/campaign rather than the entire fleet simultaneously, absent a demonstrated fleet-wide compromise path to this specific interface.

privacy.rationale: The API carries operational and user data for the affected tenant/campaign that could be exposed through an authorization flaw, not the full fleet at once absent a demonstrated fleet-wide path to this interface.

safety.rationale: The API governs remote convenience/fleet functions rather than real-time vehicle control, so its compromise does not create a direct physical safety effect.

financial.rationale: No direct financial exposure to the individual road user from API compromise itself.

operational.rationale: Loss of remote start, remote climate, or cloud-based navigation capabilities.

privacy.rationale: API responses can include the individual vehicle’s operational state and location data.

assets.name: Secure Non-Volatile Storage / Hardware Protected Partition
assets.description: Protected physical non-volatile system structures hosting core system binaries, persistent operational parameters, and localized encryption manifests.

safety.rationale: NVRAM corruption is reflected in OEM financial/operational exposure (bricked units, warranty), not a direct physical safety effect on the OEM.

financial.rationale: No Fleet-Wide-scale threat reaches Memory-class assets in this catalog (bricking/extraction requires per-device physical or local access); realistic exposure is bounded to the affected batch of devices, driving warranty/service cost rather than fleet-wide replacement.

operational.rationale: Loss of a node’s protected partition can render that ECU inoperable until re-provisioned.

privacy.rationale: The partition can hold cached credentials and encryption manifests tied to the vehicle/owner.

safety.rationale: Corruption of this generic, cross-domain storage partition can brick the hosting ECU or cause it to load an invalid configuration state, but the resulting safety effect depends on which ECU (safety-critical or not) is affected - the storage fault itself is not an actuation of any vehicle function.

financial.rationale: No direct financial exposure to the individual road user.

operational.rationale: A bricked or corrupted partition on this generic storage class disables whatever ECU function depends on it, for the affected vehicle.

privacy.rationale: Cached user credentials or profile fragments stored in this partition could be exposed if confidentiality is broken.

assets.name: Hardware Enclave / Trusted Execution Environment (TEE) Core
assets.description: Physical processor isolating secure operations, ensuring private key processing and sensitive cryptographic computations are hidden from high-level software environments.

safety.rationale: Enclave compromise is reflected in OEM financial/operational exposure, not a direct physical safety effect on the OEM.

financial.rationale: No Fleet-Wide-scale threat reaches Compute-class assets in this catalog (TEE compromise requires per-device physical or local access, not a remote/systemic path); realistic exposure is bounded to the affected trust domain's devices, not the full fleet's key-isolation architecture at once.

operational.rationale: Loss of enclave integrity forces re-keying/re-provisioning of the affected trust domain.

privacy.rationale: The enclave processes sensitive key material and can be leveraged to access protected user data if breached.

safety.rationale: The enclave underpins cryptographic trust for the node it serves; its compromise can undermine the authenticity guarantees of downstream safety-relevant operations without itself directly actuating any function.

financial.rationale: No direct financial exposure to the individual road user.

operational.rationale: Loss of enclave availability can disable cryptographic operations the node depends on to function normally.

privacy.rationale: The enclave secures sensitive key material that can protect user data; its compromise weakens that protection.

assets.name: Vehicle Immobilization Cryptographic Secret
assets.description: Pre-shared master keys or security parameters that the immobilizer validates against the key transponder before authorizing powertrain (engine/motor) activation.

safety.rationale: Immobilizer-secret compromise is reflected in OEM financial/reputational exposure (theft liability), not a direct physical safety effect on the OEM.

financial.rationale: Reputational impact and warranty/insurance claims due to easily bypassed immobilizers.

operational.rationale: Drives warranty and anti-theft system redesign costs across the affected platform.

privacy.rationale: The secret itself is not tied to personal data.

safety.rationale: Immobilizer bypass enables theft but does not itself create a physical hazard for the occupant or other road users.

financial.rationale: Key theft allows full physical bypass of anti-theft mechanics, enabling vehicle theft.

operational.rationale: Vehicle theft following immobilizer bypass results in complete loss of use of the vehicle.

privacy.rationale: The secret itself is not tied to personal data.

assets.name: Non-Safety Vehicle Comfort Configuration Profile
assets.description: Configuration metadata layouts managing peripheral user comfort bounds, actuator target mappings, and internal environmental preferences (e.g., HVAC, seating positions).

safety.rationale: This profile governs comfort-only functions and has no safety pathway for the OEM.

financial.rationale: Minor customer-service/goodwill cost from incorrect comfort settings.

operational.rationale: May generate dealer service requests to reset comfort parameters.

privacy.rationale: Comfort preferences are low-sensitivity and not linked to identity beyond the vehicle itself.

safety.rationale: Comfort parameters (HVAC, seating) have no pathway to a physical safety effect.

financial.rationale: No direct financial exposure from altered comfort settings.

operational.rationale: Annoyance due to reset seating or temperature settings.

privacy.rationale: Comfort preferences reveal minimal personal information.

assets.name: LIN Bus Data Flow
assets.description: Low-speed, master-slave bus traffic carrying switch, mirror, window, and panel status signals between body-domain nodes.

safety.rationale: LIN-bus body/comfort disruption is reflected in OEM financial/operational exposure, not a direct physical safety effect on the OEM.

financial.rationale: Minor warranty/service costs from malfunctioning body/comfort peripherals.

operational.rationale: May require dealer diagnosis of intermittent body/comfort system faults.

privacy.rationale: LIN traffic carries switch/actuator status, not personal data.

safety.rationale: Potential for minor mechanical pinching (windows/sunroof) if local hardware anti-pinch controls fail simultaneously.

financial.rationale: No direct financial exposure to the individual road user.

operational.rationale: Disrupted LIN traffic can disable windows, mirrors, or other body/comfort functions.

privacy.rationale: LIN traffic carries switch/actuator status, not personal data.

assets.name: Driver Information Display Rendering Application
assets.description: High-priority graphics application responsible for rendering critical vehicle state information - speed, warning indicators, and power/charge levels - onto the instrument cluster and other vehicle displays.

safety.rationale: Display-rendering compromise is reflected in OEM financial/operational exposure, not a direct physical safety effect on the OEM.

financial.rationale: Warranty/service cost from display malfunctions and potential regulatory scrutiny of a masked safety-relevant readout.

operational.rationale: A frozen or corrupted cluster display is a customer-facing defect typically requiring immediate dealer remediation.

privacy.rationale: The rendering application does not itself process personal data.

safety.rationale: Freezing or masking active screen outputs prevents the operator from identifying critical vehicle states or actual road velocities.

financial.rationale: No direct financial exposure to the individual road user.

operational.rationale: Loss of the primary instrument display disrupts normal driving feedback (speed, warnings, gear state).

privacy.rationale: The rendering application does not itself process personal data.

assets.name: Safety-Critical Telltale & Warning Signal Flow
assets.description: High-priority network traffic carrying safety telltale, malfunction-indicator, and restraint-system status signals across architectural domain boundaries.

safety.rationale: Suppression or falsification of safety telltales conceals active fault conditions, preventing driver corrective action and creating OEM liability for withheld safety warnings.

financial.rationale: Suppressed safety telltales expose the OEM to liability for failing to warn, and potential regulatory non-compliance (FMVSS/UNECE telltale mandates).

operational.rationale: Loss of telltale integrity undermines the OEM’s ability to rely on in-vehicle fault reporting for fleet health monitoring.

privacy.rationale: Telltale signal flow carries fault-state data, not personal data.

safety.rationale: Spoofing or dropping indicator signals blinds the road user to active platform faults, increasing operational risk profiles.

financial.rationale: No direct financial exposure to the individual road user.

operational.rationale: Suppressed or falsified telltales prevent the driver from being informed of vehicle faults requiring attention.

privacy.rationale: Telltale signal flow carries fault-state data, not personal data.

assets.name: Wireless Handset Pairing Session Keys
assets.description: Cryptographic link keys generated during mobile device pairing protocols (e.g., Bluetooth, Wi-Fi Direct) to ensure secure sessions between user devices and the vehicle's connection manager.

safety.rationale: Pairing-key compromise exposes personal data risk, not a direct physical safety effect on the OEM.

financial.rationale: Potential liability/goodwill cost tied to compromised Bluetooth pairing security.

operational.rationale: May require a security patch and re-pairing guidance rollout.

privacy.rationale: OEM liability for failing to secure Bluetooth link keys.

safety.rationale: Pairing-key compromise exposes personal communications data but has no pathway to a physical safety effect.

financial.rationale: No direct financial exposure from pairing-key compromise.

operational.rationale: No direct effect on vehicle operation.

privacy.rationale: Key extraction allows an attacker to intercept personal calls, contacts, and media playback.

assets.name: High-Bandwidth Sensor Raw Telemetry Flow
assets.description: High-throughput data pipeline carrying raw or semi-processed environmental perception streams (cameras, LiDAR, Radar) from edge arrays into central fusion processors.

safety.rationale: Sensor-feed compromise is reflected in OEM financial/operational liability exposure, not a direct physical safety effect on the OEM.

financial.rationale: No Fleet-Wide-scale threat reaches this Network-class telemetry flow in the catalog; realistic exposure is bounded to the affected vehicle/batch, driving liability and remediation cost proportionate to that scope rather than fleet-wide litigation.

operational.rationale: Disables ADAS features for the affected vehicle/batch rather than fleet-wide, absent a demonstrated Fleet-Wide-scale path to this telemetry flow.

privacy.rationale: Raw perception streams (camera/LiDAR/radar) are not linked to personal identity in this pathway.

safety.rationale: Dropping or corrupting sensor streams blinds automated driving systems, causing failure to react to physical obstacles.

financial.rationale: No direct financial exposure to the individual road user.

operational.rationale: Loss of sensor data disables ADAS/collision-avoidance features for the affected vehicle.

privacy.rationale: Raw perception streams are not linked to personal identity in this pathway.

assets.name: Active Safety Control Command Application
assets.description: Safety-critical application logic commanding immediate actuator corrections upon detecting imminent collision or lane departure vectors.

safety.rationale: Compromise of this control logic is reflected in OEM financial/operational liability exposure, not a direct physical safety effect on the OEM.

financial.rationale: A defect or compromise in active-safety control logic exposes the OEM to product-liability claims and a likely safety recall.

operational.rationale: Requires immediate feature suspension and validated patch rollout fleet-wide.

privacy.rationale: This control logic does not process personal data.

safety.rationale: Maliciously triggering or disabling this logic can force the vehicle to swerve or fail to brake in emergencies.

financial.rationale: No direct financial exposure to the individual road user.

operational.rationale: A faulted active-safety application disables collision-avoidance/lane-keeping assistance until restored.

privacy.rationale: This control logic does not process personal data.

assets.name: System Diagnostics and Operational Log Files
assets.description: Runtime operational event records, diagnostic trace strings (e.g., DLT), crash dumps, and historical telemetry generated by underlying operating systems across any compute node.

safety.rationale: The OEM as an entity has no direct physical safety state; concealment of recall-worthy fault patterns instead elevates the OEM's liability and regulatory exposure, captured under financial impact.

financial.rationale: Loss of diagnostic history complicates warranty adjudication and root-cause analysis, and delayed detection of a recall-worthy pattern increases the OEM's liability exposure if an incident occurs before the fault is identified.

operational.rationale: Diagnostic logs are the OEM’s primary field-failure visibility channel; their loss or corruption degrades fleet health monitoring.

privacy.rationale: Diagnostic logs frequently capture PII fragments (location, device identifiers) that carry data-protection obligations for the OEM if exposed.

safety.rationale: Diagnostic/log data has no pathway to a direct physical safety effect.

financial.rationale: No direct financial exposure to the individual road user.

operational.rationale: Loss of diagnostic history can delay technicians in diagnosing a road user’s vehicle fault.

privacy.rationale: Logs frequently capture plain-text location histories, API connections, and connected device identifiers.

assets.name: Cloud & Mobile App Authorization Token (OAuth/JWT)
assets.description: Bearer tokens or session cookies generated via cloud authentication used to authorize the mobile companion app and execute remote vehicle orchestration commands (e.g., remote start, unlock) via the backend.

safety.rationale: Token compromise is reflected in OEM financial/operational/privacy exposure, not a direct physical safety effect on the OEM.

financial.rationale: Account-takeover incidents drive support costs, fraud liability, and customer-trust remediation.

operational.rationale: Requires token revocation, forced re-authentication, and incident response across the affected user base.

privacy.rationale: Compromised bearer tokens grant access to the linked user’s account data and vehicle location history.

safety.rationale: Token compromise enables unauthorized remote convenience commands (unlock, start) but has no pathway to a direct physical safety effect while the vehicle is in motion.

financial.rationale: Account takeover can enable unauthorized remote unlock, facilitating theft of the vehicle or its contents.

operational.rationale: Account takeover can lock the legitimate owner out of remote vehicle functions.

privacy.rationale: Token theft allows account takeover, exposing user location history and granting remote access.

assets.name: Vehicle-to-Cloud (V2C) PKI Identity Certificate
assets.description: Cryptographic identity document facilitating transport encryption (mTLS) and ensuring mutual authentication between vehicle endpoint nodes and OEM backend infrastructures.

safety.rationale: Certificate compromise is reflected in OEM financial/operational exposure (false fleet data), not a direct physical safety effect on the OEM.

financial.rationale: Compromising the certificate allows a threat actor to impersonate the vehicle to the cloud, injecting false fleet data.

operational.rationale: Impersonation of vehicle identity can corrupt fleet telemetry and operational decision-making at the backend.

privacy.rationale: This certificate authenticates the transport channel and does not itself carry personal data.

safety.rationale: This certificate secures backend telemetry authentication and has no pathway to a direct physical safety effect.

financial.rationale: No direct financial exposure to the individual road user.

operational.rationale: Certificate compromise can disrupt cloud-dependent services (remote commands, OTA eligibility checks) for the affected vehicle.

privacy.rationale: This certificate authenticates the transport channel and does not itself carry personal data.

assets.name: Service-Oriented Architecture (SOA) Registry Middleware
assets.description: Dynamic service discovery and routing framework coordinating inter-process messaging (e.g., SOME/IP, DDS) across high-performance compute architectures and Ethernet boundaries.

safety.rationale: Registry compromise is reflected in OEM financial/operational exposure, not a direct physical safety effect on the OEM.

financial.rationale: Hijacked service discovery undermines the OEM’s SOA architecture fleet-wide, requiring urgent remediation and re-certification.

operational.rationale: A corrupted registry can misroute inter-process calls across the platform, disrupting many dependent services at once.

privacy.rationale: The registry itself does not carry personal data.

safety.rationale: Hijacking the registry can redirect service calls to a malicious endpoint, but a further step - that malicious service actually issuing harmful commands to a safety-critical function - is required before any physical effect occurs.

financial.rationale: No direct financial exposure to the individual road user.

operational.rationale: A corrupted registry can break inter-service communication the vehicle’s features depend on.

privacy.rationale: The registry itself does not carry personal data.

assets.name: Containerized Service Encapsulation Profile
assets.description: Encapsulated user-space computing instances (e.g., Docker, LXC) isolating infotainment or telematics software services from each other while sharing the underlying host OS kernel.

safety.rationale: Container-breakout compromise is reflected in OEM financial/operational exposure, not a direct physical safety effect on the OEM.

financial.rationale: A container breakout can compromise co-hosted services, raising incident-response and remediation costs.

operational.rationale: Breakout incidents require patching and redeployment of the affected container runtime fleet-wide.

privacy.rationale: A breakout can expose data belonging to co-hosted services on the same host.

safety.rationale: A breakout targets the host OS but remains isolated from physical vehicle control lines.

financial.rationale: No direct financial exposure to the individual road user.

operational.rationale: A container breakout can disrupt the infotainment or telematics services running in the affected container.

privacy.rationale: A container-level breakout targeting the host OS does not itself expose the affected service’s user data (captured under the underlying service assets).

assets.name: Diagnostic Security Access Authentication Secrets
assets.description: Seed/Key calculation algorithms and fixed secret arrays embedded within node firmware to authenticate privileged UDS diagnostic sessions (e.g., Service $27, Service $29).

safety.rationale: Secret compromise is reflected in OEM financial/operational exposure (unauthorized flashing), not a direct physical safety effect on the OEM.

financial.rationale: Extraction of UDS secrets allows unauthorized firmware flashing and parameter manipulation across the platform.

operational.rationale: Extracted UDS secrets enable unauthorized diagnostic sessions fleet-wide, undermining the OEM’s ability to control who can modify ECU parameters.

privacy.rationale: The secret itself does not carry personal data.

safety.rationale: Extraction of these secrets grants privileged UDS diagnostic access, but actually altering brake or steering calibration requires a further, separate diagnostic-session exploitation step beyond obtaining the secret itself.

financial.rationale: No direct financial exposure to the individual road user.

operational.rationale: Unauthorized diagnostic access can alter ECU parameters, requiring dealer remediation to restore correct operation.

privacy.rationale: The secret itself does not carry personal data.

assets.name: Third-Party API Keys & Service Credentials
assets.description: Static API keys or shared secrets hardcoded or provisioned in the Infotainment/Telematics systems to authenticate outbound requests to third-party cloud services (e.g., mapping providers, weather APIs, streaming media).

safety.rationale: API-key compromise is a financial/operational exposure (billing abuse), not a direct physical safety effect on the OEM.

financial.rationale: Extraction of hardcoded API keys allows attackers to abuse OEM service quotas, causing massive unexpected cloud billing.

operational.rationale: Abuse of leaked keys can force emergency key rotation across the affected service integration.

privacy.rationale: These keys authenticate service calls and do not themselves carry personal data.

safety.rationale: Third-party service API keys have no pathway to a physical safety effect.

financial.rationale: No direct financial exposure to the individual road user.

operational.rationale: Loss of service if the OEM revokes the compromised API key.

assets.description: High-bandwidth, IP-based network traffic forming the backbone of Zonal and HPC architectures, carrying SOA payloads, heavy sensor data (video/LiDAR), and inter-domain communications.

safety.rationale: Ethernet-backbone compromise is reflected in OEM financial/operational liability exposure, not a direct physical safety effect on the OEM.

financial.rationale: A demonstrated ability to disrupt the Ethernet backbone exposes the OEM to severe product-liability and regulatory consequences.

operational.rationale: Requires immediate investigation and potential stop-sale of the affected zonal/HPC architecture.

privacy.rationale: The backbone carries SOA payloads and sensor data that may include user- or vehicle-linked identifiers.

safety.rationale: Flooding the Ethernet backbone prevents ADAS perception data from reaching decision nodes, blinding autonomous systems.

financial.rationale: No direct financial exposure to the individual road user.

operational.rationale: Flooding or disrupting the backbone can disable any Ethernet-dependent function, including perception and infotainment.

privacy.rationale: This flow carries operational sensor/control data, not personal data, in this pathway.

assets.name: Cloud Backend & API Gateway Configuration
assets.description: Infrastructure definitions, API rate limits, load balancer routing rules, and cloud firewall configurations governing the OEM telematics and connected services backend environments.

safety.rationale: Backend misconfiguration is a financial/operational/privacy exposure, not a direct physical safety effect on the OEM.

financial.rationale: Misconfiguration allows Denial of Wallet attacks (autoscaling exhaustion) or fleet-wide API scraping.

operational.rationale: Misconfigured routing or rate limits can take down backend services fleet-wide.

privacy.rationale: Altering backend routing rules can expose fleet telemetry and user databases to unauthorized endpoints.

safety.rationale: Backend configuration governs cloud services rather than vehicle control, so it has no pathway to a direct physical safety effect.

financial.rationale: No direct financial exposure to the individual road user.

operational.rationale: Backend disruption can degrade or disable the cloud-dependent features (remote start, navigation) the road user relies on.

privacy.rationale: Backend misconfiguration can expose the individual road user’s account and telemetry data to unauthorized endpoints.

assets.name: ADAS Camera, Radar, and LiDAR Sensor Array
assets.description: Physical perception sensors capturing the external vehicle environment to feed machine learning algorithms and active safety functions.

safety.rationale: Sensor compromise is reflected in OEM financial/operational liability exposure, not a direct physical safety effect on the OEM.

financial.rationale: No Fleet-Wide-scale threat reaches this Peripheral-class sensor array in the catalog; realistic remediation cost is bounded to the affected batch of vehicles rather than a fleet-wide firmware/hardware campaign, absent a demonstrated remote/systemic path.

operational.rationale: Sensor faults typically require dealer recalibration or replacement of the affected unit.

privacy.rationale: Raw sensor hardware output is not linked to personal identity in this pathway.

safety.rationale: Compromised or spoofed sensors can cause the vehicle to misinterpret obstacles, leading to collisions.

financial.rationale: No direct financial exposure to the individual road user.

operational.rationale: Spoofed or degraded sensor input disables or restricts ADAS features for the affected vehicle.

privacy.rationale: Raw sensor hardware output is not linked to personal identity in this pathway.

assets.name: Powertrain Electromechanical Actuators
assets.description: Physical edge hardware components (e.g., electronic throttle bodies) responsible for actuating drive torque commands.

safety.rationale: Actuator compromise is reflected in OEM financial/operational liability exposure, not a direct physical safety effect on the OEM.

financial.rationale: A demonstrated actuator-level compromise exposes the OEM to product-liability claims and a hardware recall.

operational.rationale: Triggers investigation and potential stop-sale for the affected vehicle/batch rather than an immediate fleet-wide action, absent a demonstrated Fleet-Wide-scale path to this Peripheral-class asset.

privacy.rationale: Electromechanical actuators do not process personal data.

safety.rationale: Unauthorized manipulation of acceleration actuators directly results in fatal vehicle behavior.

financial.rationale: No direct financial exposure to the individual road user.

operational.rationale: Manipulated actuator behavior directly disrupts normal throttle response.

privacy.rationale: Electromechanical actuators do not process personal data.

assets.name: In-Cabin Microphones & Multimedia Capture Devices
assets.description: Physical multimedia peripherals used for voice commands, hands-free calling, and video conferencing.

safety.rationale: Microphone/camera compromise is a privacy exposure, not a direct physical safety effect on the OEM.

financial.rationale: Regulatory fines for privacy violations.

operational.rationale: Requires incident response and potential feature disablement pending a fix.

privacy.rationale: Unauthorized microphone/camera access captures highly sensitive in-cabin audio/video of occupants.

safety.rationale: Eavesdropping via cabin microphones/cameras has no pathway to a physical safety effect.

financial.rationale: No direct financial exposure to the individual road user.

operational.rationale: No direct effect on vehicle operation.

privacy.rationale: Eavesdropping on private conversations within the vehicle cabin.

assets.name: Telematics Control Unit (TCU) Hardware Platform
assets.description: Physical compute hardware hosting the cellular modem, GNSS receiver, and telematics software stack. Acts as the primary vehicle-to-cloud communication gateway and the physical entry point for all wireless back-channel attacks.

safety.rationale: TCU compromise is reflected in OEM financial/operational/privacy exposure, not a direct physical safety effect on the OEM.

financial.rationale: No Fleet-Wide-scale threat reaches Compute-class assets in this catalog; while the TCU is the primary remote-access vector, compromising the hardware platform itself requires a per-device local/physical path, bounding realistic remediation cost to the affected batch rather than large-scale fleet attacks.

operational.rationale: Disables V2C connectivity, OTA, eCall, and fleet management for the affected batch of vehicles rather than fleet-wide simultaneously, absent a demonstrated Fleet-Wide-scale path to this Compute-class asset.

privacy.rationale: TCU handles raw GNSS location data and user traffic, exposing location history and communication metadata.

safety.rationale: TCU is not directly in the control path but provides a remote attack surface that, when chained with CGW vulnerabilities, can reach safety ECUs.

financial.rationale: No direct financial exposure to the individual road user from TCU compromise itself.

operational.rationale: Loss of eCall, navigation, and remote assistance degrades road safety services.

privacy.rationale: Vehicle location and trip data are continuously processed by the TCU.

assets.name: Physical Diagnostic Access Interface
assets.description: Physical connectors and test pads providing direct wired access to vehicle networks and ECU debug interfaces. Includes the standardized OBD-II Data Link Connector (DLC), JTAG/SWD boundary-scan pads, and UART console interfaces exposed on PCBs. Primary vector for physical-proximity attacks.

safety.rationale: Physical diagnostic access is reflected in OEM financial/operational exposure (IP theft, tuning), not a direct physical safety effect on the OEM.

financial.rationale: Physical diagnostic access is the root vector for in-depth reverse engineering, IP theft, and aftermarket tuning that undermines OEM revenue and warranty control.

operational.rationale: Attackers with physical access can brick ECUs, corrupt calibration data, or install persistent backdoors requiring costly dealer interventions.

privacy.rationale: Diagnostic sessions expose stored PII, trip logs, and paired device credentials accessible from the DLC.

safety.rationale: This is a physical access point; reaching a safety-relevant outcome (disabling a safety system, injecting malicious commands) requires a further exploitation step through the exposed protocols (UDS/JTAG/CAN) once physical access is obtained - the port itself does not actuate any function.

financial.rationale: OBD-based relay attacks and immobilizer bypasses are a primary vehicle theft vector.

operational.rationale: Malicious calibration or firmware flashing via the diagnostic port can leave the vehicle inoperable or unsafe.

privacy.rationale: Trip data, linked account tokens, and PII may be extractable via the DLC without authentication.

assets.name: In-Vehicle Network Intrusion Detection & Prevention System (IDS/IPS)
assets.description: Software or hardware-assisted monitoring agent analyzing in-vehicle network traffic (CAN, Automotive Ethernet) for anomalous message patterns, unauthorized frame injection, or statistical deviations indicative of an ongoing cyber attack. Mandated by UNECE WP.29 R155 for type-approved vehicles.

safety.rationale: IDS/IPS compromise is reflected in OEM financial/operational exposure (loss of detection capability), not a direct physical safety effect on the OEM.

financial.rationale: IDS compromise undermines UNECE R155 compliance posture and removes forensic evidence needed for incident response, increasing regulatory and litigation exposure.

operational.rationale: An IDS taken offline loses all alerting and telemetry, disabling the security operations capability and leaving the vehicle exposed.

privacy.rationale: IDS processes raw network traffic which may contain sensitive signals or PII fragments; its data store must be protected.

safety.rationale: IDS failure is not immediately safety-impacting but removes detection of in-progress attacks that may escalate to safety-critical systems.

financial.rationale: No direct financial exposure to the individual road user.

operational.rationale: Indirect impact through reduced security posture; direct operational impact on the driver is minimal.

privacy.rationale: The IDS processes network traffic but does not itself expose the individual road user’s personal data.

assets.name: Driver Monitoring System (DMS) Biometric Sensor & Data
assets.description: In-cabin near-infrared camera and associated inference engine monitoring driver gaze direction, eyelid closure, head pose, and physiological state to detect drowsiness, distraction, or medical impairment. Processes biometric data and feeds active safety interventions. Mandated by Euro NCAP 2026 and EU GSR2 for L2+ vehicles.

safety.rationale: DMS compromise is reflected in OEM financial/operational/privacy exposure, not a direct physical safety effect on the OEM.

financial.rationale: DMS data breach exposes highly sensitive biometric data triggering GDPR and biometric privacy regulations with significant regulatory fines.

operational.rationale: DMS failure disables L2+ hands-off functionality and regulatory compliance triggers service lockout of conditional automation features.

privacy.rationale: DMS continuously captures facial biometrics and physiological indicators are among the most sensitive PII categories under GDPR and equivalent regulations.

safety.rationale: DMS is the primary sensor for detecting driver drowsiness, distraction, or impairment that gates L2+ automated-driving safety interventions; spoofing or disabling it directly removes that detection function while the system continues to assume normal driver engagement.

financial.rationale: No direct financial exposure to the individual road user.

operational.rationale: DMS failure may disable automated driving features the driver relies upon.

privacy.rationale: Unauthorized access to continuous biometric face and eye-tracking data constitutes a severe personal privacy violation.

assets.name: FPGA Configuration Bitstream
assets.description: Proprietary hardware configuration bitstream defining the FPGA fabric logic used for radar signal processing, sensor fusion preprocessing, or custom automotive protocol bridging. Contains synthesized IP core definitions that deterministically program the device gate-level logic at power-on. Stored in external SPI flash or on-die configuration memory.

safety.rationale: Bitstream compromise is reflected in OEM financial/operational exposure (IP theft, counterfeiting), not a direct physical safety effect on the OEM.

financial.rationale: Extraction of the bitstream constitutes direct IP theft of proprietary hardware logic - the synthesized netlist cannot be re-derived without the original RTL source.

operational.rationale: Cloning of the bitstream enables counterfeit hardware production that bypasses OEM supply chain controls.

privacy.rationale: The bitstream is hardware configuration logic and does not carry personal data.

safety.rationale: Modification of the radar or LiDAR preprocessing bitstream corrupts sensor pipeline outputs at the gate level, ahead of any software-layer sanity checks or redundancy mechanisms.

financial.rationale: No direct financial exposure to the individual road user.

operational.rationale: A corrupted bitstream degrades sensor-fusion input quality, restricting or disabling the ADAS features that depend on it.

privacy.rationale: The bitstream is hardware configuration logic and does not carry personal data.

assets.name: Event Data Recorder (EDR) / Crash Data Recorder
assets.description: Dedicated, tamper-evident non-volatile storage module that captures a fixed pre-crash and post-crash data snapshot - vehicle speed, throttle/brake application, seatbelt status, airbag/restraint deployment, and steering angle - triggered once a crash-severity threshold is met (e.g., a longitudinal or lateral velocity change exceeding 8 km/h within 150 ms, or non-reversible restraint deployment). Once a locking event is recorded, the snapshot is protected against overwrite for the legally mandated retention window, supporting post-incident forensic reconstruction and liability determination - and is consequently a frequent target for tampering to conceal fault evidence.

safety.rationale: None: the EDR is a passive recorder and the OEM has no direct physical-safety state; the exposure from falsified or lost crash data (post-market surveillance, litigation) is carried in oem.financial.

financial.rationale: No Fleet-Wide-scale threat reaches Memory-class assets in this catalog; EDR tampering/unavailability is realized per-device via physical or local access, so litigation and type-approval exposure is bounded to the affected batch rather than dispositive-evidence loss across the fleet at once.

operational.rationale: Undermines the OEM's post-crash forensic and recall-investigation workflows.

privacy.rationale: EDR records are linkable to an identifiable vehicle/owner and are subject to data-protection obligations when retrieved for investigation.

safety.rationale: The recorder does not participate in real-time vehicle control; its compromise cannot itself cause a crash or unsafe maneuver.

financial.rationale: A tampered or unavailable EDR record can cause a driver to be wrongly assigned fault in a collision, with direct consequences for insurance liability and legal exposure.

operational.rationale: No effect on normal, day-to-day vehicle operation.

privacy.rationale: Crash-triggered snapshots reveal driving behavior (speed, braking, belt use) at the time of an incident - sensitive, but limited in scope and duration compared to continuously captured telemetry.

assets.notes: Regulatory basis: UN R160 (light vehicles, M1/N1), UN R169/EU 2024/2220 (heavy vehicles, M2/M3/N2/N3), and 49 CFR Part 563 (US). Domain modeled as "*" because the recorder aggregates a cross-domain data snapshot (powertrain, chassis, and body signals) rather than serving a single bus segment.

assets.name: EV Charging Communication Controller (EVCC)
assets.description: Vehicle-side compute module implementing the ISO 15118 communication stack: the SLAC (Signal Level Attenuation Characterization) matching procedure that pairs the vehicle to a specific charging outlet over HomePlug GreenPHY power-line communication, the TLS/PKI-secured session negotiation with the charging station's SECC (Supply Equipment Communication Controller), and the higher-layer V2G/ISO 15118-20 message exchange - charging-parameter negotiation, Plug & Charge authentication, and bidirectional V2G power scheduling. Relays negotiated charging commands and authorization state to the Battery Management System (BMS) and Vehicle Control Unit (VCU).

safety.rationale: None: the OEM has no direct physical-safety state; liability for an unsafe charging condition caused by a compromised EVCC is expressed in oem.financial (recall, warranty and liability exposure).

financial.rationale: EVCC compromise enabling billing/session fraud or contributing to a safety recall carries direct financial and warranty exposure.

operational.rationale: EVCC failure halts the vehicle's ability to charge, a core function OEMs are contractually and reputationally obligated to support.

privacy.rationale: EVCC session logs and Plug & Charge identifiers can reveal charging location and timing patterns tied to a specific vehicle.

safety.rationale: Malicious manipulation of negotiated charging current/voltage parameters can, in the worst case, contribute to a thermal event at the battery or charge port.

financial.rationale: A compromised EVCC can be leveraged for charging-session or billing fraud, or a bricked EVCC leaves the owner unable to charge - both with direct cost to the owner.

operational.rationale: Loss of EVCC functionality strands an EV without its primary means of refueling.

privacy.rationale: Charging-session data reveals the vehicle's location and schedule over time.

assets.notes: Distinct from A.032 (EVSE Plug & Charge Billing Credentials), which models only the cryptographic contract-certificate artifact, not the compute platform that terminates the protocol.

assets.name: Infotainment USB/Media Port (Physical Interface)
assets.description: The physical USB-A/USB-C receptacle(s) in the cabin and the associated host-side media-handling stack: mass-storage and MTP device drivers, the automatic media/file parsers invoked on insertion, and wired CarPlay/Android Auto accessory-mode negotiation. Also serves as the dealer/technician firmware-loading interface for infotainment software updates in some architectures. As a physically exposed, driver/passenger-accessible port with no inherent trust boundary on what is plugged in, it is a primary vector for removable-media attacks.

safety.rationale: None: infotainment USB compromise does not directly reach safety-critical control loops and the OEM has no direct physical-safety state; any exposure is expressed in oem.financial and oem.operational.

financial.rationale: Exploitation typically manifests as warranty claims, reputational damage from demonstrated attacks, or data-exfiltration disclosure costs rather than large-scale fleet liability.

operational.rationale: Malware persistence introduced via USB can require a dealer re-flash to fully remediate.

privacy.rationale: USB-based extraction of paired-phone contacts, call/SMS logs, and navigation history synced to infotainment is a well-documented data-exfiltration path with regulatory exposure for the OEM.

safety.rationale: Direct control-loop impact from an infotainment-only compromise is unlikely, though driver distraction from a manipulated infotainment UI is a secondary concern.

financial.rationale: Limited direct financial exposure to the individual road user.

operational.rationale: Malware introduced via USB can degrade or crash the infotainment system, disabling navigation, the backup-camera display, or hands-free calling.

privacy.rationale: The infotainment head unit routinely stores a paired phone's contact list, call history, and messages; USB-based exfiltration exposes this directly to the individual road user.

assets.notes: The "USB" and "Media Slots" metadata tags are already referenced by T.09.4 and T.19.6 but, prior to this entry, were unused across the asset catalog.

assets.name: V2X On-Board Unit (OBU)
assets.description: Dedicated V2X radio module - a DSRC (IEEE 802.11p) and/or C-V2X (3GPP PC5 sidelink) chipset, an application processor running the V2X message stack (BSM/CAM generation and validation), a positioning co-processor, an IEEE 1609.2/ETSI TS 103 097 security co-processor performing pseudonym-certificate signing and verification, and a dedicated 5.9 GHz antenna - that transmits and receives V2X safety messages (collision warnings, intersection movement assist, road-hazard signaling) to and from other vehicles and roadside infrastructure.

safety.rationale: None: the OEM has no direct physical-safety state; liability and recall exposure from false hazard warnings sent to receiving vehicles is carried in oem.financial.

financial.rationale: V2X safety-message integrity failures are tied to regulatory homologation (IEEE 1609.2/ETSI TS 103 097) and carry significant liability and recall exposure.

operational.rationale: OBU failure disables cooperative-safety features (intersection movement assist, V2V forward collision warning) without disabling the vehicle itself.

privacy.rationale: Even with pseudonym rotation, OBU compromise or misuse can degrade the anonymity set and enable movement tracking.

safety.rationale: The OBU's entire purpose is safety messaging; a spoofed or jammed OBU can directly cause the receiving vehicle or driver to brake, swerve, or fail to react to a genuine hazard.

financial.rationale: No material financial exposure to the road user from OBU compromise itself.

operational.rationale: Loss of cooperative-awareness features degrades, but does not eliminate, the vehicle's basic drivability.

privacy.rationale: V2X messages broadcast position, speed, and heading in the clear (only the signing identity is pseudonymous); a compromised OBU can undermine the location-privacy protection pseudonym rotation is meant to provide.

assets.notes: Distinct from A.033 (V2X Pseudonym Certificates, the crypto artifact) and A.063 (TCU Hardware Platform, scoped to Cellular/GNSS only, with no V2X radio chain).

assets.name: Digital Key UWB/BLE Ranging Anchor Module
assets.description: The in-cabin and exterior array of Ultra-Wideband (IEEE 802.15.4z / Car Connectivity Consortium Digital Key 3.0) anchor radios, together with the BLE radios used for initial connection and out-of-band pairing, that perform time-of-flight distance measurement to physically localize and authenticate the proximity of a paired smartphone or digital key credential before authorizing PEPS-style unlock and engine start.

safety.rationale: None: the ranging module gates convenience unlock/start, not a safety-critical control loop, and the OEM has no direct physical-safety state; theft exposure is expressed in oem.financial.

financial.rationale: UWB ranging was adopted specifically to defeat BLE/LF relay-attack theft; a demonstrated bypass undermines the OEM's anti-theft value proposition and marketing claims, with associated warranty and reputational cost.

operational.rationale: Ranging-module malfunction can cause nuisance lockouts or failure of passive entry, a common source of dealer service visits.

privacy.rationale: The ranging hardware itself does not process or store personally identifiable data beyond transient distance measurements.

safety.rationale: Compromise of the ranging function does not itself endanger occupants or other road users.

financial.rationale: A successful relay or distance-spoofing attack against the ranging function results in complete vehicle theft, identical in financial consequence to any other keyless-entry bypass.

operational.rationale: Loss of use of the vehicle following theft, or nuisance failure to unlock/start following ranging-module malfunction.

privacy.rationale: No PII is exposed by compromise of the ranging hardware itself.

assets.notes: Distinct from A.004 (Vehicle Access Authorization Token), the cryptographic session artifact these ranging measurements gate.

assets.name: In-Cabin Conversational AI / LLM Copilot Interface
assets.description: An in-cabin, large-language-model-based voice/chat assistant integrated with vehicle functions (climate control, navigation, messaging, remote-start) via tool-calling/function-calling access that lets it invoke real vehicle commands based on natural-language user intent. Ingests external context - web search results it retrieves on the user's behalf, calendar entries, navigation POI descriptions, and received messages - as part of forming its responses. Distinct from the perception/ADAS machine-learning models hosted on A.040 (tagged `ML Model / Weights`): this is an agentic, tool-calling conversational system that reasons over natural language and unstructured external content to decide which vehicle functions to invoke, not a passive inference model operating on sensor tensors.

safety.rationale: Per the catalog's OEM-safety methodology, whatever safety-adjacent exposure the OEM carries from a compromised copilot is a consequence of road-user harm, expressed monetarily below (financial/operational) - the OEM itself has no direct physical safety state a compromise can affect.

financial.rationale: A demonstrated prompt-injection exploit that unlocks vehicles or exfiltrates conversation data at scale carries significant liability, recall, and reputational exposure, comparable to other Fleet-Wide-reachable Infotainment-domain compromises.

operational.rationale: Responding to a disclosed jailbreak/injection technique typically forces urgent guardrail patches, tightened tool-calling permission scopes, or temporary suspension of the assistant's vehicle-control functions fleet-wide.

privacy.rationale: Conversation transcripts and the external content the assistant ingests (calendar entries, messages) may be logged for model improvement or support, carrying data-protection obligations for the OEM or its LLM backend provider.

safety.rationale: The assistant's tool-calling can directly actuate door-unlock, climate, and messaging functions without a further exploitation chain, which is a real safety-adjacent risk (e.g. unexpected unlock or distraction while driving). It is rated Moderate rather than Severe because none of its exposed functions reach braking, steering, or powertrain control loops - consistent with how this catalog calibrates other indirect/non-control-loop actuation risks.

financial.rationale: A manipulated assistant that unlocks the vehicle enables theft, and one that sends messages or triggers purchases/subscriptions on the user's behalf enables fraud, both with direct cost to the owner.

operational.rationale: Unwanted actions (an unintended unlock, a sent message, a changed climate/navigation setting) disrupt normal use and erode trust in the assistant, without disabling the vehicle itself.

privacy.rationale: The assistant's conversation history routinely reflects highly personal content - calendar entries, message contents, location intent, and habits inferred from natural-language requests - whose exfiltration is a severe, direct privacy exposure to the individual user.

assets.notes: Hosted on A.041 (Cockpit / Infotainment Domain Controller). Relies on A.062 (In-Cabin Microphones) for voice input and A.029 (Third-Party API Keys & Service Credentials) for the outbound calls it makes to external services (web search, navigation POI lookups). Deliberately excludes the `ML Model / Weights` metadata tag to keep this asset distinct from A.040's perception/ADAS inference models - see T.01.14 (LLM/Conversational AI Prompt Injection) for the primary threat this asset introduces.

assets.name: Powertrain Actuation Command Flow
assets.description: High-priority, deterministic network traffic carrying motor torque setpoints to physical control actuators.

safety.rationale: Actuation-command compromise is reflected in OEM financial/operational liability exposure, not a direct physical safety effect on the OEM.

financial.rationale: A demonstrated spoofing of actuation commands exposes the OEM to product-liability claims and a recall.

operational.rationale: Triggers investigation and a possible stop-sale for the affected vehicles.

privacy.rationale: This traffic carries control setpoints, not personal data.

safety.rationale: Spoofing or delaying these signals causes unintended acceleration or loss of drive torque.

financial.rationale: No direct financial exposure to the individual road user.

operational.rationale: Disrupting this traffic directly interferes with normal acceleration response.

privacy.rationale: This traffic carries control setpoints, not personal data.

assets.name: Chassis Electromechanical Actuators
assets.description: Physical edge hardware components (e.g., brake calipers, steering motors) responsible for actuating braking and steering commands.

safety.rationale: Actuator compromise is reflected in OEM financial/operational liability exposure, not a direct physical safety effect on the OEM.

financial.rationale: A demonstrated actuator-level compromise exposes the OEM to product-liability claims and a hardware recall.

operational.rationale: Triggers investigation and a possible stop-sale for the affected vehicles.

privacy.rationale: Electromechanical actuators do not process personal data.

safety.rationale: Unauthorized manipulation of braking or steering actuators directly results in fatal vehicle behavior.

financial.rationale: No direct financial exposure to the individual road user.

operational.rationale: Manipulated actuator behavior directly disrupts normal brake or steering response.

privacy.rationale: Electromechanical actuators do not process personal data.
